notes: Phase C extraction for agent-builder UX teardown (Flowise, Langflow, Dify, Gumloop, Coze). Focus: agent-vs-graph-chat UX confusion antipattern. Evidence grounded in 38 T0-T3 sources spanning official product pages, documentation, GitHub repos, practitioner analyses (Elestio production-ready, Toolhalla comparison, Hatchworks agent patterns), and academic HCI studies. Metrics sourced from: (1) official UI/UX documentation (Dify workflow nodes, Langflow visual editor, Flowise canvas), (2) practitioner teardowns noting pane/click patterns, (3) agent design pattern literature (Luke Wroblewski on orchestration UI, Agentic Design Patterns library, RAGExplorer visual analytics). Row targets per PLAN: ~25 screens, 5 flows, ~12 patterns. Coverage: up to 5 products × ~1-2 screens + ~1-2 flows per product, plus shared antipatterns.

ux_screens.description: Primary drag-and-drop node-based editor for composing LLM chains. Displays multiple nodes (LLM, retrieval, tools) connected via edges on an infinite canvas. Left sidebar contains component palette; right inspector pane shows node configuration.
Modal overlay for configuring agent behavior (tools, memory, reasoning loops). Lacks clear indication of agent-vs-query execution mode; conflates chat-style interactions with orchestration planning.

Node-and-edge visual programming interface for building LangChain workflows. Component library tree on left, large canvas center with real-time execution preview. Requires extensive clicking to configure node parameters.

Multi-paned debugging interface showing code preview, test output, and logs. Agent step-through results mixed with function call traces; unclear distinction between plan-then-execute vs conversational agent patterns.

Comprehensive node-based workflow builder with typed nodes (LLM, knowledge retrieval, code execution, conditionals). Clear node I/O contracts. Canvas emphasizes data flow over chat; supports branching and loops.
Multi-step wizard for RAG pipeline setup (embedding model, chunking strategy, retrieval parameters). Modal dialogs with form validation; 2-3 clicks per configuration decision.

Drag-and-drop module-based builder emphasizing AI-first automation. Modules (API calls, AI steps, conditionals) arranged linearly or in decision trees. Integration palette on left; execution preview on right.
Configuration modal for deploying agent to Slack/Teams. Mixes workflow configuration with chat interface settings; unclear whether user is building an orchestrated agent or a conversational chatbot.
ByteDance Coze Studio node-based bot builder. Supports multi-model selection, knowledge base attachments, and workflow orchestration. Canvas-first design with plugin ecosystem.
Settings interface for uploading and configuring knowledge bases (documents, web scrapers, API sources). Table-based document list; bulk operations modal.
Iframe preview of embeddable chat widget. Displays conversation thread; unclear whether user is testing orchestrated agent plan execution or simple Q&A.
Dual-pane interface: left shows agent execution trace (step name, input/output, tool calls), right shows conversation preview. Clear separation of orchestration view vs end-user chat.

ux_flows.goal: User creates, tests, and deploys a multi-step LLM workflow (e.g., RAG pipeline with tool calls)

steps.action: Drag LLM node from palette to canvas
steps.friction: Requires opening collapse/expand tree; palette is small

steps.action: Click LLM node to open property inspector; select model + API key
steps.friction: Modal dialog within modal; credential management unclear

steps.action: Drag retrieval node (vector store); connect edge from LLM input
steps.friction: Edge routing is automatic but can obscure other nodes; connection handles require precise cursor

steps.action: Configure vector store credentials and chunk strategy
steps.friction: Settings scattered across multiple modals; no inline validation

steps.action: Add tool/function node for external API call
steps.friction: Tool library search is basic; no filtering by use-case

steps.action: Click 'Run' to test end-to-end; inspect execution logs
steps.friction: Logs are text-based; unclear which step failed; no breakpoint debugging

steps.action: Toggle 'Agent Mode' for agentic behavior; configure tool selection strategy
steps.friction: Agent-vs-workflow distinction is unclear; modal UI mixes configuration concerns

steps.action: Deploy to Flowise cloud or self-hosted; obtain embed code
steps.friction: Deployment wizard has >5 steps; credential re-entry required; lack of progress indicator

ux_flows.our_approach: MetroGraph reduces click count to 12 by: (1) inline property editing with autocomplete, (2) unified agent/workflow configuration in right inspector with clear visual distinction, (3) one-click deploy using pre-configured credentials, (4) execution trace as integrated overlay (not separate modal) with clickable steps.

ux_flows.goal: User diagnoses why agent took wrong action or failed; traces root cause through LLM reasoning + tool calls

steps.action: Trigger workflow with test input; wait for execution
steps.friction: No inline test interface; must switch to separate test panel

steps.action: Inspect execution tab; scroll through logs to find failure point
steps.friction: Logs are chronological flat list; no tree/hierarchy; timestamps only, no execution flow diagram

steps.action: Click on tool-call step to see tool definition + input/output
steps.friction: Tool definition is mixed with runtime data; hard to distinguish config vs execution state

steps.action: Trace back to LLM step to inspect prompt + reasoning tokens
steps.friction: Must click multiple nested toggles; reasoning data is raw JSON; no highlighting of key decisions

steps.action: Modify component (e.g., change LLM temperature) in main graph view
steps.friction: Graph is hidden behind logs; must minimize log pane or open separate window

steps.action: Re-run workflow to test fix; compare old vs new execution traces
steps.friction: No diff view; must manually compare logs side-by-side

steps.action: Export execution trace for documentation/debugging; save as snapshot
steps.friction: No export option; copy-paste only; trace format is not standardized

ux_flows.our_approach: MetroGraph shows execution as annotated flow diagram (not logs) with: (1) step duration, input/output, status (success/fail) as node overlays, (2) collapsible nested steps for multi-level tool calls, (3) inline diff highlighting changed parameters between runs, (4) one-click capture of trace snapshot.

ux_flows.goal: User creates a chatbot that answers questions using uploaded knowledge base

steps.action: Create new workflow; drag LLM and knowledge-retrieval nodes to canvas
steps.friction: Low; node library is searchable and well-organized

steps.action: Connect retrieval output to LLM input using drag-to-drop edge
steps.friction: Minimal; connection handles are visually distinct; auto-layout prevents overlap

steps.action: Click knowledge node; upload PDF and configure embedding model
steps.friction: Inline form within inspector; file upload with progress indicator; embedding model selection has helpful defaults

steps.action: Configure LLM node: select model, set system prompt, adjust temperature
steps.friction: Inspector provides tooltips; settings are categorized (core vs advanced)

steps.action: Test workflow with sample query; inspect retrieval results + LLM response
steps.friction: Execution trace shows retrieval hits + context window; step outputs are JSON but formatted readably

steps.action: Publish workflow; generate shareable link; embed in website
steps.friction: One-click publish; pre-configured iframe embed code; no additional setup required

ux_flows.our_approach: Dify's orchestration-first design (not chat-first) is our model. MetroGraph extends this by: (1) visual retrieval quality scoring (heatmap of token overlap between query + retrieved docs), (2) side-by-side view of retrieval window during live test, (3) versioning of knowledge base snapshots for reproducible RAG results.

ux_flows.goal: User creates an automation that triggers on Slack messages and runs AI-powered workflow

steps.action: Create new automation; drag Slack trigger module to canvas
steps.friction: Slack trigger is pre-built; minimal config (just scopes)

steps.action: Drag AI/LLM module; configure prompt template with slack_message variable
steps.friction: Variable binding is text-based (no visual binding); requires manual {{variable}} syntax

steps.action: Drag action module (e.g., send reply); map LLM output to Slack message
steps.friction: Module palette search is slow; module count (130+) makes discovery hard

steps.action: Test automation by simulating Slack message; review output
steps.friction: Test modal requires manual input; no replay of recent Slack messages; execution logs are minimal

steps.action: Deploy to Slack; configure agent persona and response settings
steps.friction: Agent vs workflow distinction blurred; persona config (tone, style) mixed with automation logic

ux_flows.our_approach: MetroGraph provides: (1) visual data flow (inputs/outputs color-coded by type), (2) template variables auto-discovered from trigger context, (3) execution preview showing Slack message before send, (4) clear visual labels distinguishing 'Automation orchestration' pane from 'Agent personality' settings.

ux_flows.goal: User builds agent supporting multiple LLMs, uploads knowledge base, and publishes to web + WeChat

steps.action: Select bot template (e.g., 'QA Bot'); configure name and description
steps.friction: Template selection is straightforward; defaults are sensible

steps.action: Upload knowledge base (document set, URL crawler, or API); configure indexing
steps.friction: File upload is chunked and resumable; indexing happens async with progress indicator

steps.action: Configure model selection; choose primary + fallback LLMs from multi-model registry
steps.friction: Model selector is clear; Coze's model inventory is comprehensive

steps.action: Add plugins (tools) via Coze marketplace; configure tool settings
steps.friction: Plugin discovery is catalog-based; one-click install

steps.action: Test agent in embedded chat preview; iterate on system prompt
steps.friction: Live preview updates without refresh; system prompt editor shows token count

steps.action: Publish to web, WeChat, and Feishu simultaneously; obtain deployment link
steps.friction: One-click multi-platform deployment; pre-configured OAuth flows

ux_flows.our_approach: Coze's multi-platform deployment is strong. MetroGraph adds: (1) per-platform preview panels (show how agent renders on each channel), (2) channel-specific behavior rules (e.g., WeChat character limits), (3) A/B testing UI for model/prompt variants across channels.

ux_patterns.pattern: Agent Orchestration vs Conversational Chat Mode Conflation
ux_patterns.description: Platforms blur the distinction between agentic orchestration (plan-then-execute, tool sequences, step-wise reasoning) and chat interface (turn-taking conversation, reactive Q&A). Users mistake 'agent deployment' for simple chatbot building, leading to misaligned expectations about autonomy, reasoning transparency, and failure modes.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph separates orchestration view (graph-based, step-centric, plan visibility) from conversation view (turn-based, role-centric). Users explicitly choose mode; UI changes to match (e.g., execution trace shown for orchestration, conversation history for chat).

ux_patterns.description: Nested modals for node configuration, credential entry, and advanced settings. Users lose context of the overall workflow; no inline editing; each config change requires click-modal-edit-close cycle.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph uses right-side inspector pane (persistent, scrollable) for all configuration. Modal reserved for destructive actions (delete) or complex workflows (multi-step wizard). Inline editing with autocomplete reduces modal dependency.

ux_patterns.pattern: Flat Execution Logs for Debugging Multi-Step Workflows
ux_patterns.description: Execution traces shown as chronological flat logs (timestamps, messages, raw JSON). No hierarchical structure; hard to trace causal chain through nested tool calls, retries, and conditional branches.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph renders execution as annotated flow diagram: nodes show status (success/fail/running), duration, input/output. Nested steps collapse/expand. Diff view highlights changes between runs.

ux_patterns.pattern: Large Tool/Integration Library with Poor Discovery
ux_patterns.description: Platforms support 50+ integrations (APIs, tools, services) but discovery is limited to search bar or flat list. Users don't know what's available; no categorization by use-case, domain, or integration type.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph organizes tools into: (1) function-based categories (data, AI, external service), (2) use-case-based workflows (e.g., 'RAG Pipeline' bundles retrieval + embedding + reranking), (3) recently-used favorites. Search includes natural-language intent matching ('extract emails' → email parser tool).

ux_patterns.pattern: Node-Based Workflow Editors with High Surface Area (many panes)
ux_patterns.description: Best-in-class platforms (Dify, Coze) use multi-pane layouts: canvas center, node library left, inspector right, execution trace bottom/overlay. This spreads UI across screen; requires attention switching. However, pane reduction risks losing functionality (e.g., hiding execution trace forces separate window).
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph reduces to 2 stable panes (canvas + inspector) with: (1) floating panels for rare operations (publish, import), (2) modal-only for wizards, (3) execution trace as collapsible overlay on canvas (not separate bottom pane). Pane count stays 2-3 (vs Langflow's 4+).

ux_patterns.pattern: Chat-First UI for Agent Systems (violates agent UX principles)
ux_patterns.description: Some platforms default to chat interface for agent testing/deployment. This hides agent reasoning (plan, tool selection, reasoning steps). Users see only final response; confusion when agent misbehaves because internals are opaque.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph's test interface shows orchestration trace alongside chat output: when user queries agent, they see the plan (which tools were called, in what order), reasoning (why tool X was chosen), and fallbacks (if plan failed, what was retried). Chat interface is secondary, not primary.

ux_patterns.description: Modern agentic design patterns emphasize visibility: before execution, show the agent's plan (which steps it will take, which tools it will use). During execution, show progress (current step, tool calls). On failure, highlight the step that failed and why.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph adopts this pattern: (1) 'Plan Mode' button shows what agent intends to do (as DAG of steps), (2) during test run, step-by-step animation of execution, (3) failure highlighting shows which step failed + error message + suggested fixes.

ux_patterns.pattern: Visual Analytics for RAG Pipeline Diagnosis
ux_patterns.description: RAG systems often fail silently (wrong documents retrieved, poor reranking, LLM confabulation). Academic systems (RAGExplorer) and observability tools (Langfuse, Arize Phoenix) address this with comparative visualization: show candidate documents, retrieval scores, reranking decisions, final context window sent to LLM.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph embeds RAG observability: (1) retrieval results shown with relevance heatmap (token overlap visualization), (2) side-by-side view of original query, retrieved docs, and LLM response, (3) one-click to swap reranking algorithm and re-run (no graph edit required).

ux_patterns.pattern: Multi-Model Orchestration (LLM model selection per step)
ux_patterns.description: Platforms (Coze, Dify) allow choosing different LLM models for different workflow steps (e.g., GPT-4 for reasoning, Haiku for classification). This enables cost optimization and model specialization but increases configuration complexity.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph adopts this: each LLM node shows model selector with defaults. Tooltip explains cost/latency tradeoff. Global 'Use cheaper model' button swaps all models to Haiku (with warning on capability loss).

ux_patterns.pattern: Execution Trace as Flow Diagram (vs flat logs)
ux_patterns.description: Instead of chronological logs, show execution as annotated graph: nodes represent steps, edges show data flow. Each node displays status (success/fail/running), duration, input/output. This mirrors the workflow structure.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph renders execution as overlay on the workflow graph itself (same visual structure as definition). Steps light up as they execute; final state persists for inspection.

ux_patterns.description: Platforms require credentials for LLM APIs, vector stores, external services. Credential entry scattered across: node configuration modals, workspace settings, .env files (self-hosted). Users struggle with credential scope (global vs per-node) and rotation.
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph centralizes credentials: (1) one 'Credentials' panel (accessible via sidebar button), (2) credential type auto-detected from LLM model selection, (3) per-credential scope toggle (global workspace vs single workflow), (4) credential rotation with version history (no orphaned references).

ux_patterns.pattern: Lack of Version Control for Workflows
ux_patterns.description: Most platforms lack version control. Users can't easily: (1) revert bad changes, (2) compare old vs new workflow, (3) branch for experimentation, (4) merge team edits. Fork-and-branch workflows are manual (copy-paste).
ux_patterns.our_rationale: MetroGraph embeds version control: (1) every publish creates a snapshot, (2) branching via 'Create variant' button, (3) diff view shows what changed since last version, (4) one-click rollback to prior version.
